proofs.proof_tex:
Throughout, \(1\leq\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1<\infty\), as required by the declared parameter spaces.  Write \(V=(Y(0),Y(1))\), and define \(\operatorname{logit}(s)=\log\{s/(1-s)\}\) for \(0<s<1\).

First let \(\widetilde P\in\mathcal M^{\circ}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\).  Strict positivity in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}positive\text{-}common\text{-}u\text{-}class}\) makes every conditional probability below an element of \((0,1)\).  Define
\[
e_{u,x}=\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=u,X=x),
\qquad
b_x=\operatorname{logit}(e_{0,x}),
\]
and
\[
\alpha_x=\operatorname{logit}(e_{1,x})-
          \operatorname{logit}(e_{0,x}).
\]
Because \(u\in\{0,1\}\), these definitions give the binary-logistic coordinate identity
\[
\operatorname{logit}\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=u,X=x)
=b_x+\alpha_xu.                                           \tag{1}
\]
Put \(s_{u,x}=\widetilde P(U=u,X=x)>0\).  Then the definition of \(\zeta\) gives
\[
\zeta_{1,u,x}=s_{u,x}e_{u,x},
\qquad
\zeta_{0,u,x}=s_{u,x}(1-e_{u,x}).                         \tag{2}
\]
Cancelling the positive factor \(s_{0,x}s_{1,x}\) in (2) yields
\[
\frac{\zeta_{1,1,x}\zeta_{0,0,x}}
     {\zeta_{1,0,x}\zeta_{0,1,x}}
=\frac{e_{1,x}(1-e_{0,x})}{e_{0,x}(1-e_{1,x})}
=\exp(\alpha_x).                                          \tag{3}
\]
Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}odds\text{-}upper}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}odds\text{-}lower}\), together with positivity of the denominator in (3), are therefore equivalent to
\[
\Gamma_A^{-1}\leq\exp(\alpha_x)\leq\Gamma_A,
\]
and monotonicity of the logarithm makes this equivalent to
\[
|\alpha_x|\leq\log\Gamma_A.                              \tag{4}
\]

For the outcome coordinates, use the declared risks
\(\mu_{a,u,x}=\widetilde P\{Y(a)=1\mid U=u,X=x\}\) and define
\[
c_{a,x}=\operatorname{logit}(\mu_{a,0,x}),
\qquad
\delta_{a,x}=\operatorname{logit}(\mu_{a,1,x})-
              \operatorname{logit}(\mu_{a,0,x}).
\]
Again because \(u\) is binary,
\[
\operatorname{logit}\widetilde P\{Y(a)=1\mid U=u,X=x\}
=c_{a,x}+\delta_{a,x}u.                                   \tag{5}
\]
The definition of \(\eta\) gives
\[
\eta_{a,1,u,x}=s_{u,x}\mu_{a,u,x},
\qquad
\eta_{a,0,u,x}=s_{u,x}(1-\mu_{a,u,x}).                   \tag{6}
\]
Cancelling \(s_{0,x}s_{1,x}>0\) in (6) gives
\[
\frac{\eta_{a,1,1,x}\eta_{a,0,0,x}}
     {\eta_{a,1,0,x}\eta_{a,0,1,x}}
=\frac{\mu_{a,1,x}(1-\mu_{a,0,x})}
       {\mu_{a,0,x}(1-\mu_{a,1,x})}
=\exp(\delta_{a,x}).                                     \tag{7}
\]
Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}outcome\text{-}odds\text{-}upper}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}outcome\text{-}odds\text{-}lower}\) are consequently equivalent, on the positive chart, to
\[
|\delta_{a,x}|\leq\log\Gamma_a.                          \tag{8}
\]

Conversely, suppose a strictly positive full-data law satisfies the observed-margin, consistency, and latent-ignorability conditions in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}positive\text{-}common\text{-}u\text{-}class}\), and admits (1) and (5) with (4) and (8).  Reversing (3) and (7) proves all four weak cross-product inequalities in that definition.  The law therefore belongs to \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\).  The two implications prove the asserted union equality.  The intercepts \(b_x\) and \(c_{a,x}\) may range over \(\mathbb R\), subject only to the requirement that, together with the law of \((X,U)\) and a strictly positive conditional coupling of \(V\), the resulting law obey the fixed observed margin.  Thus this is an internal reparameterization of the maintained class.

We next prove the closure assertion without assigning an odds ratio at a null cell.  Let \(C\subseteq\Delta_{\mathrm{full}}\) be the set of nonnegative full-data tables satisfying the observed-margin and consistency restrictions, the following division-free form of latent ignorability,
\[
\widetilde P(v,a,u,x)\widetilde P(u,x)
=\widetilde P(v,u,x)\widetilde P(a,u,x)                  \tag{9}
\]
for every \(v\in\{0,1\}^2\), \(a,u\in\{0,1\}\), and \(x\in\mathcal X\), and the four declared weak joint-cell inequalities in \(\zeta\) and \(\eta\).  Here the observed-margin and consistency restrictions state that the pushforward under
\[
(x,a,u,y_0,y_1)\longmapsto(x,a,ay_1+(1-a)y_0)
\]
equals \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).  These pushforward restrictions are linear equalities in the full-table cells, (9) is a finite family of polynomial equalities, and the inequalities in \(\zeta\) and \(\eta\) are polynomial weak inequalities because \(\zeta\) and \(\eta\) are linear marginalizations of the full table.  Hence \(C\) is closed in the finite-dimensional simplex.  Every law in \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\) lies in \(C\), so Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}common\text{-}u\text{-}class}\) gives
\[
\mathcal M
=\operatorname{cl}_{\Delta_{\mathrm{full}}}\mathcal M^{\circ}
\subseteq C.                                              \tag{10}
\]

For the reverse inclusion, fix \(\widetilde P\in C\).  We construct strictly positive laws in the maintained class converging cellwise to \(\widetilde P\).  Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\).  By the declared support conditions, \(\lambda_x>0\), \(0<p_x<1\), and \(0<r_{a,x}<1\).  Thus
\[
w_{a,x}=\widetilde P(U=1\mid A=a,X=x)
\]
is well defined, and the treatment cells are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\zeta_{1,1,x}&=\lambda_xp_xw_{1,x},
&\zeta_{1,0,x}&=\lambda_xp_x(1-w_{1,x}),\\
\zeta_{0,1,x}&=\lambda_x(1-p_x)w_{0,x},
&\zeta_{0,0,x}&=\lambda_x(1-p_x)(1-w_{0,x}).
\end{aligned}                                             \tag{11}
\]
Cancelling \(\lambda_x^2p_x(1-p_x)>0\) in the two treatment inequalities gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
w_{1,x}(1-w_{0,x})
&\leq\Gamma_Aw_{0,x}(1-w_{1,x}),\\
w_{0,x}(1-w_{1,x})
&\leq\Gamma_Aw_{1,x}(1-w_{0,x}).
\end{aligned}                                             \tag{12}
\]
Because \(\Gamma_A<\infty\), (12) implies the exhaustive alternative
\[
0<w_{0,x},w_{1,x}<1,
\qquad (w_{0,x},w_{1,x})=(0,0),
\qquad\text{or}\qquad(w_{0,x},w_{1,x})=(1,1).            \tag{13}
\]
Indeed, setting either coordinate equal to zero in the inequality having the other coordinate on its left forces both to be zero; setting either coordinate equal to one in the other inequality forces both to be one.  All remaining pairs are interior.

Consider first the interior case in (13).  Both values of \(U\) then have positive probability given \(X=x\), and every \((A,U,X=x)\)-cell is positive.  Equation (9) implies that the conditional table
\[
g_{u,x}(y_0,y_1)
=\widetilde P\{V=(y_0,y_1)\mid U=u,X=x\}
\]
is also the conditional table of \(V\) given \((A=a,U=u,X=x)\), for either \(a\).  Define its armwise marginals by
\[
\mu_{a,u,x}=\sum_{y_0,y_1}y_a g_{u,x}(y_0,y_1).
\]
Consistency, the observed-margin restriction, and (9) imply
\[
r_{a,x}=(1-w_{a,x})\mu_{a,0,x}+w_{a,x}\mu_{a,1,x}.       \tag{14}
\]
Writing \(\rho_{u,x}=\widetilde P(U=u\mid X=x)>0\), the outcome cells are
\[
\eta_{a,1,u,x}=\lambda_x\rho_{u,x}\mu_{a,u,x},
\qquad
\eta_{a,0,u,x}=\lambda_x\rho_{u,x}(1-\mu_{a,u,x}).      \tag{15}
\]
After cancelling \(\lambda_x^2\rho_{0,x}\rho_{1,x}>0\), the two outcome inequalities become
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_{a,1,x}(1-\mu_{a,0,x})
&\leq\Gamma_a\mu_{a,0,x}(1-\mu_{a,1,x}),\\
\mu_{a,0,x}(1-\mu_{a,1,x})
&\leq\Gamma_a\mu_{a,1,x}(1-\mu_{a,0,x}).
\end{aligned}                                             \tag{16}
\]
Equations (14)--(16) and \(0<r_{a,x}<1\) imply
\[
0<\mu_{a,0,x},\mu_{a,1,x}<1.                             \tag{17}
\]
To verify the lower inequalities in (17), if either risk in (16) were zero, the inequality with the other risk on its left would force that other risk to be zero, contradicting (14).  For the upper inequalities, if either risk were one, the inequality with the complementary factor on its right would force the other risk to be one, again contradicting (14).

Let \(h_{u,x}\) be the product-Bernoulli table having the same two marginals as \(g_{u,x}\):
\[
h_{u,x}(y_0,y_1)
=\prod_{a=0}^1
 \mu_{a,u,x}^{y_a}(1-\mu_{a,u,x})^{1-y_a}.               \tag{18}
\]
By (17), every cell of \(h_{u,x}\) is positive.  For \(0<\varepsilon<1\), set
\[
g_{u,x}^{(\varepsilon)}
=(1-\varepsilon)g_{u,x}+\varepsilon h_{u,x}.             \tag{19}
\]
This table is strictly positive and has the same two Bernoulli marginals as \(g_{u,x}\).  Keep the \((A,U,X)\)-table fixed and use \(g_{u,x}^{(\varepsilon)}\) as the conditional law of \(V\) for both treatment values.  This preserves (9), the observed binary outcome margins through (14), and every \(\zeta\)- and \(\eta\)-inequality through (11) and (15), while making every full-data cell in this stratum positive.

It remains to treat a constant-confounder case in (13); write its constant value as \(c\in\{0,1\}\).  Since both treatment arms have positive probability and (9) holds, there is a common conditional table
\[
g_{c,x}(y_0,y_1)
=\widetilde P\{V=(y_0,y_1)\mid U=c,X=x\},
\]
whose arm-\(a\) marginal equals \(r_{a,x}\), by consistency and the observed-margin restriction.  Let
\[
h_x(y_0,y_1)
=\prod_{a=0}^1 r_{a,x}^{y_a}(1-r_{a,x})^{1-y_a}.          \tag{20}
\]
Every cell of \(h_x\) is positive.  For \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), define
\[
\widetilde P^{(\varepsilon)}(U=c\mid A=a,X=x)=1-\varepsilon,
\qquad
\widetilde P^{(\varepsilon)}(U=1-c\mid A=a,X=x)=\varepsilon, \tag{21}
\]
and set
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_{\widetilde P^{(\varepsilon)}}(V\mid U=c,X=x)
&=(1-\varepsilon)g_{c,x}+\varepsilon h_x,\\
\mathcal L_{\widetilde P^{(\varepsilon)}}(V\mid U=1-c,X=x)
&=h_x,
\end{aligned}                                             \tag{22}
\]
using each conditional law in (22) for both values of \(A\).  Equations (20)--(22) make every full-data cell positive and impose (9).  Both conditional tables in (22) have arm-\(a\) risk \(r_{a,x}\), so the observed margin is unchanged.  Equation (21) makes the treatment cross-product ratio equal to one, and equality of the armwise risks across the two values of \(U\) makes every outcome cross-product ratio equal to one.  Since each budget is at least one, all four weak inequalities hold.  Moreover, (21)--(22) converge cellwise to the original constant-\(U\) table as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).

Apply (19) in every interior stratum and (21)--(22) in every constant-\(U\) stratum.  Finiteness of \(\mathcal X\) lets these constructions be combined, with the masses \(\lambda_x\) and the \((A,X)\)-margin fixed, into one law \(\widetilde P^{(\varepsilon)}\).  The binary outcome risks \(r_{a,x}\), propensities \(p_x\), and stratum masses \(\lambda_x\) characterize the observed law, so the observed-margin restriction is exact.  Every full-data cell is positive, and the law satisfies consistency, latent ignorability, and the four declared odds inequalities.  Therefore
\[
\widetilde P^{(\varepsilon)}
\in\mathcal M^{\circ}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1),
\qquad
\widetilde P^{(\varepsilon)}\longrightarrow\widetilde P
\quad\text{cellwise}.                                    \tag{23}
\]
Thus \(C\subseteq\operatorname{cl}_{\Delta_{\mathrm{full}}}\mathcal M^{\circ}=\mathcal M\).  Together with (10), this proves \(C=\mathcal M\).  Every boundary step used only polynomial equalities and weak joint-cell inequalities, so no conditional odds ratio was evaluated at a null cell.  Finally, because the argument compares no distinct historical model class, it establishes neither equality nor inclusion with any class considered in Rosenbaum--Rubin Sections 2--4, exactly as claimed.

Fix (x\in\mathcal X).  We treat the two stated boundary regimes separately.

First suppose that (Gamma_A=1).  By Definition (mathrm{def{:}exposure  ext{-}region}), every ((w_0,w_1)\in D_{A,x}) obeys
\[
w_1(1-w_0)\leq w_0(1-w_1)
\quad\text{and}\quad
w_0(1-w_1)\leq w_1(1-w_0).
\]
The two cross-products are therefore equal.  Expanding and cancelling their common term gives
\[
w_1-w_0w_1=w_0-w_0w_1,
\qquad\text{hence}\qquad
w_1=w_0.
\]
This algebra remains valid at the boundary values (0) and (1).  Write the common value as (w_x).  The prevalence formula in Definition (mathrm{def{:}adjusted  ext{-}arm  ext{-}mean}) then yields
\[
\pi_x=p_xw_x+(1-p_x)w_x=w_x=w_{a,x},
\qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For every feasible outcome-odds value (  heta>0), Definition (mathrm{def{:}adjusted  ext{-}arm  ext{-}mean}) consequently gives
\[
q_{a,x}(w_x,w_x;\theta)-r_{a,x}
=(\pi_x-w_{a,x})(m_1-m_0)=0.
\]
Thus, by Definition (mathrm{def{:}common  ext{-}u  ext{-}endpoints}),
\[
q^-_{a,x}(w_x,w_x)=q^+_{a,x}(w_x,w_x)=r_{a,x}
\]
and
\[
H^-_x(w_x,w_x)=H^+_x(w_x,w_x)=r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}.
\]
Because every point of (D_{A,x}) is diagonal when (Gamma_A=1), both endpoint objectives are constant on the whole feasible region.  Hence
\[
\ell_x=\upsilon_x=r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}.
\]
Summing over the finite support (mathcal X), as prescribed by Definition (mathrm{def{:}common  ext{-}u  ext{-}endpoints}), proves
\[
L=R=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\lambda_x(r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}).
\]
The strictly positive pair (w_{0,x}=w_{1,x}=1/2) belongs to (D_{A,x}).  The exact equality for both the interior and closed maintained classes in Theorem (mathrm{thm{:}sharp  ext{-}common  ext{-}u  ext{-}envelope}) therefore shows that this singleton, rather than merely an outer bound, is the causal ATE identified set and that its endpoint is attained in the interior class.

Now suppose that (Gamma_0=Gamma_1=1).  Then (Gamma_a=1) for each (a\in\{0,1\}).  Take any
\(widetilde P\in\mathcal M^{\circ}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,1,1)\), and fix ((a,x)).  Define
\[
c_{u,x}=\widetilde P(U=u,X=x),
\qquad u\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Strict positivity in Definition (mathrm{def{:}positive  ext{-}common  ext{-}u  ext{-}class}) implies
\[
c_{u,x}>0
\quad\text{and}\quad
0<\mu_{a,u,x}<1.
\]
Definitions of (eta) and (mu) give the factorizations
\[
\eta_{a,1,u,x}=c_{u,x}\mu_{a,u,x},
\qquad
\eta_{a,0,u,x}=c_{u,x}(1-\mu_{a,u,x}).
\]
Assumptions (mathrm{ass{:}outcome  ext{-}odds  ext{-}upper}) and (mathrm{ass{:}outcome  ext{-}odds  ext{-}lower}), specialized to (Gamma_a=1), supply the two opposite inequalities and hence the equality
\[
\eta_{a,1,1,x}\eta_{a,0,0,x}
=\eta_{a,1,0,x}\eta_{a,0,1,x}.
\]
Substitution of the preceding factorizations gives
\[
c_{1,x}c_{0,x}\mu_{a,1,x}(1-\mu_{a,0,x})
=c_{0,x}c_{1,x}\mu_{a,0,x}(1-\mu_{a,1,x}).
\]
Division by the strictly positive quantity (c_{0,x}c_{1,x}), followed by expansion and cancellation, yields
\[
\mu_{a,1,x}-\mu_{a,1,x}\mu_{a,0,x}
=\mu_{a,0,x}-\mu_{a,0,x}\mu_{a,1,x},
\qquad\text{so}\qquad
\mu_{a,1,x}=\mu_{a,0,x}.
\]
It remains to identify this common risk.  Assumption (mathrm{ass{:}observed  ext{-}margin}) and the definition of (r_{a,x}) imply
\[
r_{a,x}=\widetilde P(Y=1\mid A=a,X=x).
\]
Assumption (mathrm{ass{:}consistency}) replaces (Y) by (Y(a)) on ({A=a}), while Assumption (mathrm{ass{:}latent  ext{-}ignorability}) removes (A) from the conditional potential-outcome distribution given ((X,U)).  The law of total probability therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
r_{a,x}
&=\widetilde P\{Y(a)=1\mid A=a,X=x\}\\
&=\sum_{u=0}^1
  \widetilde P\{Y(a)=1\mid A=a,U=u,X=x\}
  \widetilde P(U=u\mid A=a,X=x)\\
&=\sum_{u=0}^1
  \mu_{a,u,x}\widetilde P(U=u\mid A=a,X=x)\\
&=\mu_{a,0,x}\sum_{u=0}^1
  \widetilde P(U=u\mid A=a,X=x)
=\mu_{a,0,x}.
\end{aligned}
\]
All displayed conditional probabilities and all divisions used above are well defined because (widetilde P) lies in the strictly positive class; in particular, every ((A=a,U=u,X=x)) cell has positive mass.  We have proved, for every ((a,x)),
\[
\mu_{a,0,x}=\mu_{a,1,x}=r_{a,x}.
\]
Equivalently, (  heta_{a,x}=1) on the strictly positive chart.  This conclusion also follows through the mixture parameterization: Definition (mathrm{def{:}mixture  ext{-}root}) and Lemma (mathrm{lem{:}binary  ext{-}mixture  ext{-}inversion}) give
\[
\kappa(r_{a,x},w_{a,x},1)=r_{a,x},
\qquad m_0=m_1=r_{a,x}.
\]
Since the interval ([Gamma_a^{-1},Gamma_a]) is now the singleton ({1}), Definition (mathrm{def{:}adjusted  ext{-}arm  ext{-}mean}) yields, for every strictly positive feasible posterior pair,
\[
q_{a,x}(w_0,w_1;1)
=r_{a,x}+(\pi_x-w_{a,x})(r_{a,x}-r_{a,x})
=r_{a,x}.
\]
It follows from Definition (mathrm{def{:}common  ext{-}u  ext{-}endpoints}) that
\[
H^-_x(w_0,w_1)=H^+_x(w_0,w_1)=r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}
\]
on the strictly positive part of (D_{A,x}).  Proposition (mathrm{prop{:}closed  ext{-}chart  ext{-}extension}) extends both objectives continuously to all of the compact region (D_{A,x}), including the constant-(U) corners.  Every boundary pair is a limit of strictly positive feasible pairs; hence continuity preserves the displayed constant value on all of (D_{A,x}).  Therefore
\[
\ell_x=\upsilon_x=r_{1,x}-r_{0,x},
\qquad
L=R=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\lambda_x(r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}).
\]
Finally, (w_{0,x}=w_{1,x}=1/2) is strictly positive and feasible.  Theorem (mathrm{thm{:}sharp  ext{-}common  ext{-}u  ext{-}envelope}) identifies the images of both (mathcal M^{\circ}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,1,1)) and its closed extension with ([L,R]).  Thus the displayed singleton is the exact, interior-attained ATE identified set in the second regime as well.

Let \(n\mapsto(\Gamma_{A,n},\Gamma_{0,n},\Gamma_{1,n})\) be a sequence in \([1,\infty)^3\) such that every coordinate tends to infinity, and let \(L_n,R_n\) denote the functionals in \(\mathrm{def{:}common\text{-}u\text{-}endpoints}\) evaluated at these budgets.  We prove convergence of the two endpoints.

First we derive a budget-free outer bound by worst-case completion of the two unobserved treatment-response means.  Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\).  For a compatible full-data law put
\[
 s_{1,x}=\widetilde E\{Y(1)\mid A=0,X=x\},
 \qquad
 s_{0,x}=\widetilde E\{Y(0)\mid A=1,X=x\}.
\]
The conditions \(0<p_x<1\) and \(\lambda_x>0\) make these conditional expectations well defined, and binary outcomes imply \(0\leq s_{a,x}\leq1\).  Observed-law compatibility and consistency give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widetilde E\{Y(1)\mid X=x\}
   &=p_xr_{1,x}+(1-p_x)s_{1,x},\\
 \widetilde E\{Y(0)\mid X=x\}
   &=(1-p_x)r_{0,x}+p_xs_{0,x}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore
\[
 b_x^-:=p_xr_{1,x}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}-p_x
 \leq \widetilde E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x\}
 \leq p_xr_{1,x}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}+1-p_x=:b_x^+.
 \tag{1}
\]
The observed-margin and consistency restrictions are closed equalities in the finite-dimensional cell probabilities.  Thus (1) also holds for every law in the closure \(\mathcal M\) from \(\mathrm{def{:}common\text{-}u\text{-}class}\).  Since \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}common\text{-}u\text{-}envelope}\) identifies \([L_n,R_n]\) with the exact image of \(\tau\) over that closed class, weighting (1) by \(\lambda_x\) and summing over the finite set \(\mathcal X\) yields
\[
 B^-:=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\lambda_xb_x^-
 \leq L_n\leq R_n\leq
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\lambda_xb_x^+=:B^+.
 \tag{2}
\]

We next give feasible common-confounder sequences approaching both inequalities in (2).  Define
\[
 \varepsilon_n=\frac{1}{1+\sqrt{\Gamma_{A,n}}},
 \qquad
 w_{1,x}^{(n)}=1-\varepsilon_n,
 \qquad
 w_{0,x}^{(n)}=\varepsilon_n
 \tag{3}
\]
for every \(x\).  These prevalences lie in \((0,1)\), converge respectively to one and zero, and satisfy
\[
 \frac{w_{1,x}^{(n)}(1-w_{0,x}^{(n)})}
      {w_{0,x}^{(n)}(1-w_{1,x}^{(n)})}
 =\left(\frac{1-\varepsilon_n}{\varepsilon_n}\right)^2
 =\Gamma_{A,n}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Hence (3) belongs to \(D_{A,x}\): the upper treatment-odds inequality is an equality and the lower one follows from \(\Gamma_{A,n}^{-1}\leq\Gamma_{A,n}\).  Its marginal confounder prevalence is
\[
 \pi_x^{(n)}=p_x(1-\varepsilon_n)+(1-p_x)\varepsilon_n\longrightarrow p_x.
 \tag{5}
\]
Bayes' formula, whose denominators are positive by (3) and \(0<p_x<1\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widetilde P_n(A=1\mid U=1,X=x)
 &=\frac{p_x(1-\varepsilon_n)}
         {p_x(1-\varepsilon_n)+(1-p_x)\varepsilon_n}
 \longrightarrow1,\\
 \widetilde P_n(A=1\mid U=0,X=x)
 &=\frac{p_x\varepsilon_n}
         {p_x\varepsilon_n+(1-p_x)(1-\varepsilon_n)}
 \longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
This verifies explicitly the asserted loss of latent treatment positivity.

For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), a positive number \(\vartheta\), and the posterior prevalence \(w_{a,x}^{(n)}\), set
\[
 m_{a,0,x}^{(n)}(\vartheta)
   =\kappa(r_{a,x},w_{a,x}^{(n)},\vartheta),
 \qquad
 m_{a,1,x}^{(n)}(\vartheta)
   =\frac{\vartheta m_{a,0,x}^{(n)}(\vartheta)}
          {1+(\vartheta-1)m_{a,0,x}^{(n)}(\vartheta)}.
 \tag{7}
\]
Binary-mixture inversion, as incorporated in the sharp-envelope result, shows that both risks are in \((0,1)\) and that
\[
 r_{a,x}=(1-w_{a,x}^{(n)})m_{a,0,x}^{(n)}(\vartheta)
          +w_{a,x}^{(n)}m_{a,1,x}^{(n)}(\vartheta),
 \qquad
 \frac{m_{a,1,x}^{(n)}(\vartheta)}
      {1-m_{a,1,x}^{(n)}(\vartheta)}
 =\vartheta
  \frac{m_{a,0,x}^{(n)}(\vartheta)}
       {1-m_{a,0,x}^{(n)}(\vartheta)}.
 \tag{8}
\]
The positivity of the four denominators in (8) follows from the interior-risk conclusion.

We now establish the needed limits directly from (8).  If \(w_{a,x}^{(n)}\to1\), then
\[
 \left|m_{a,1,x}^{(n)}(\vartheta_n)-r_{a,x}\right|
 =(1-w_{a,x}^{(n)})
  \left|m_{a,1,x}^{(n)}(\vartheta_n)
        -m_{a,0,x}^{(n)}(\vartheta_n)\right|
 \leq1-w_{a,x}^{(n)}.
 \tag{9}
\]
If \(w_{a,x}^{(n)}\to0\), the analogous identity gives
\[
 \left|m_{a,0,x}^{(n)}(\vartheta_n)-r_{a,x}\right|
 \leq w_{a,x}^{(n)}.
 \tag{10}
\]
Because \(r_{a,x}\in(0,1)\), equations (8)--(10), continuity of the odds map on \((0,1)\), and divergence of the outcome budgets imply that on the lower branch \(\vartheta_{a,n}=\Gamma_{a,n}\),
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
 m_{1,1,x}^{(n)}(\Gamma_{1,n})\longrightarrow r_{1,x},
 &m_{1,0,x}^{(n)}(\Gamma_{1,n})\longrightarrow0,\\
 m_{0,0,x}^{(n)}(\Gamma_{0,n})\longrightarrow r_{0,x},
 &m_{0,1,x}^{(n)}(\Gamma_{0,n})\longrightarrow1.
\end{array}
\tag{11}
\]
For example, the first limit is (9), and then the second odds in (8) equal the first odds divided by \(\Gamma_{1,n}\), which tends to zero.  The control-arm limits follow from (10), after which multiplication of the limiting positive finite odds by \(\Gamma_{0,n}\) makes the other odds diverge.  On the upper branch \(\vartheta_{a,n}=\Gamma_{a,n}^{-1}\), the same calculation gives
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
 m_{1,1,x}^{(n)}(\Gamma_{1,n}^{-1})\longrightarrow r_{1,x},
 &m_{1,0,x}^{(n)}(\Gamma_{1,n}^{-1})\longrightarrow1,\\
 m_{0,0,x}^{(n)}(\Gamma_{0,n}^{-1})\longrightarrow r_{0,x},
 &m_{0,1,x}^{(n)}(\Gamma_{0,n}^{-1})\longrightarrow0.
\end{array}
\tag{12}
\]

It remains to verify that these algebraic branches are attained by compatible laws.  For each \(n\), each of the two branches, and every stratum, define the \((X,A,U)\) margin by
\[
 \widetilde P_n(X=x,A=a,U=u)
 =\lambda_xp_x^a(1-p_x)^{1-a}
  \{w_{a,x}^{(n)}\}^{u}\{1-w_{a,x}^{(n)}\}^{1-u}.
 \tag{13}
\]
Conditionally on \((X=x,U=u)\), let \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) be independent Bernoulli variables with the respective success probabilities in (7), use the same conditional law for both values of \(A\), and set \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\).  Every cell of this full-data law is strictly positive because \(\lambda_x>0\), \(0<p_x<1\), (3) is interior, and all risks in (7) lie in \((0,1)\).  The construction makes \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid(X,U)\) and enforces consistency.  The mixture equality in (8) reproduces each observed risk \(r_{a,x}\), so the binary observed margin is \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).  Equation (4) verifies both treatment-odds restrictions.  In the outcome cross-product ratio, the factors \(\lambda_x\pi_x^{(n)}\) and \(\lambda_x(1-\pi_x^{(n)})\) cancel, leaving exactly the conditional-risk odds ratio in (8), which is either \(\Gamma_{a,n}\) or \(\Gamma_{a,n}^{-1}\); thus both outcome-odds restrictions hold.  Consequently each constructed law belongs to \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\).

Under either branch its adjusted arm mean satisfies
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widetilde E_n\{Y(a)\mid X=x\}-r_{a,x}
 &=\bigl[(1-\pi_x^{(n)})m_{a,0,x}^{(n)}
          +\pi_x^{(n)}m_{a,1,x}^{(n)}\bigr]\\
 &\quad-\bigl[(1-w_{a,x}^{(n)})m_{a,0,x}^{(n)}
          +w_{a,x}^{(n)}m_{a,1,x}^{(n)}\bigr]\\
 &=(\pi_x^{(n)}-w_{a,x}^{(n)})
   (m_{a,1,x}^{(n)}-m_{a,0,x}^{(n)}),
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
which is precisely the adjusted-arm map used by \(\mathrm{def{:}common\text{-}u\text{-}endpoints}\).  Combining (5), (11), and the first line of (14), the lower-branch stratum contrast tends to
\[
 p_xr_{1,x}-\{(1-p_x)r_{0,x}+p_x\}=b_x^-.
 \tag{15}
\]
Combining (5), (12), and (14), the upper-branch stratum contrast tends to
\[
 \{p_xr_{1,x}+1-p_x\}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}=b_x^+.
 \tag{16}
\]
The construction is simultaneous over the finite support \(\mathcal X\), so its stratum limits may be weighted by \(\lambda_x\) and summed.  Let \(\widetilde P_n^-\) and \(\widetilde P_n^+\) denote the resulting lower- and upper-branch laws.  Their feasibility and exact sharpness give
\[
 B^-\leq L_n\leq\tau(\widetilde P_n^- )\longrightarrow B^-,
 \qquad
 B^+\geq R_n\geq\tau(\widetilde P_n^+ )\longrightarrow B^+.
\]
Thus \(L_n\to B^-\) and \(R_n\to B^+\).  Endpoint convergence is equivalent to Hausdorff convergence of these compact intervals, proving
\[
 [L_n,R_n]\longrightarrow
 \left[
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\lambda_x\{p_xr_{1,x}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}-p_x\},
 \ \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\lambda_x\{p_xr_{1,x}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}+1-p_x\}
 \right].
\]
The proof uses divergence of both outcome budgets in (11)--(12), divergence of the treatment budget in (3)--(4), and the vanishing latent propensities in (6).  It therefore establishes only the stated all-budget, vanishing-positivity limit and makes no finite-budget recovery claim.

proposed.statement: Let all three budgets diverge and allow a sequence of compatible laws with \(w_{1,x}\to1\), \(w_{0,x}\to0\), \(\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=1,X=x)\to1\), and \(\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=0,X=x)\to0\).  Then \([L,R]\) converges to the binary-outcome Manski interval \(\left[\sum_x\lambda_x\{p_xr_{1,x}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}-p_x\},\;\sum_x\lambda_x\{p_xr_{1,x}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}+1-p_x\}\right]\).  No Manski-recovery claim is made at finite budgets or under latent positivity bounded away from zero.
proposed.justification: The all-budget limit locates the model between point identification and unrestricted treatment-response bounds without overstating finite-budget coverage.
proposed.gap: Imbens relates unrestricted sensitivity to worst-case bounds qualitatively; this proposition gives the exact common-binary-\(U\) endpoint limit and the required loss of latent positivity.
proposed.consumer: Users can interpret very large budgets against a familiar worst-case benchmark and detect implementations that converge to the wrong limit.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof directly uses the observed-margin, consistency, latent-ignorability, treatment-odds, and outcome-odds restrictions to construct interior compatible laws, as well as the exposure-region, mixture-root, adjusted-mean, and binary-mixture-inversion nodes.  Adding these direct edges makes the declared proof spine complete; the claim is unchanged.
